conceptZh: 身體腹部，裝食物的地方。
object: a round fuzzy gachapon pocket creature, a giant toy belly-button capsule, and a tiny mini snack
morph: creature balloons huge and shrinks to fit parts of 肚
creativeAngle: 扭蛋小怪獸吃到巨大點心，肚子變超大又縮小；肚臍冒出。
promptEn: An 8-second silly animated clip, bright pastel look, soft daylight, no dark grading. On a bubble-gum pink and cream playmat, a round fuzzy pocket creature bursts from a gachapon capsule and bounces next to a gigantic cookie that is bigger than it is. 0–1.5s: The creature tries to hold the cookie, the first 肚 is spoken, and it squishes underneath, squeaking, only a pair of ears sticking out. 1.5–3.1s: It gobbles a corner and its belly swells like a balloon; the second 肚 is spoken as the belly bounces it across the mat. 3.1–4.7s: A hiccup shrinks the belly back into the cookie crumbs, which scatter and snap into the 肚 glyph in warm brown. 4.7–5.7s: As 肚臍 is spoken, the creature lifts its shirt-like fluff and a perfect little round belly button winks, giving a tiny giggle wiggle. Final hold (about 5.0–8.0s): the creature pats its belly in a happy beat while crumbs sparkle; the glyph does not move. Audio: a warm off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly this line, slowly and distinctly with the marked tones, then stops: 肚、肚、肚臍（ㄉㄨˋ、ㄉㄨˋ、ㄉㄨˋ ㄑㄧˊ）. The first 肚 lands at about 0.9s, the second 肚 at about 2.5s, and the word 肚臍 at about 4.8s, each timed to the picture described above. Keep 肚 as the one and only piece of writing on screen, a bold saturated color against a pale bright background, correctly formed with every stroke legible; nothing else is written anywhere. The glyph 肚 fills roughly 70% of frame height, centered and uncropped, and stays perfectly still for the final 3 seconds while the lead keeps playing away from the strokes. No real people, no flashing.

conceptZh: 肚子，身體裝食物、會鼓起來的地方。
object: one long stretchy orange astronaut snack tube that two hungry characters tug between them
morph: the tube is stretched to its limit and snaps into two bouncing lengths: the left length folds into the 月 half and the right length folds into the 土 half, landing together as the glyph 肚
creativeAngle: 改走「拔河」笑點：太空人玩偶和小外星人各抓住一條橘色太空點心管的兩端互拉，太空人老是飄起來、撞到飛碟底部，最後點心管「啪」地彈開，兩人跌坐在地，彈開的兩段分別折成「月」和「土」組成「肚」。念「肚子」時太空人摸摸圓鼓鼓的肚子，聲音和畫面同一件事。與上一版撲滿豬、小毛怪吃餅乾完全不同。
promptEn: An 8-second slapstick animated clip, bright pastel look, soft even daylight, no dark grading. Setting: a flat pale cream-and-sky-blue toy moon mat with a few soft bumps, nothing busy behind. Lead: a bouncy toy astronaut figure with a round fishbowl helmet, white puffy suit and a big friendly cartoon face, who keeps floating off the ground at the wrong moment. Supporting character: a small green cartoon alien in a tiny toy flying saucer with a wobbly tractor beam. 0 to 1.4s: a long stretchy orange snack tube lies in the middle of the mat. The astronaut lands with a bounce on the left, eyes go wide, it rubs its empty flat tummy and points at the tube; the first 肚 is spoken at about 0.9s as it lunges for the near end. 1.4 to 3.0s: the moment it grabs, it drifts straight up with the tube end in its hands, legs pedalling in the air, and bonks its fishbowl helmet on the underside of the saucer hovering in from the right; the helmet wobbles with a soft boing, and the alien's tractor beam locks onto the far end of the tube. 3.0 to 4.3s: tug-of-war. Astronaut on the left, saucer on the right, the orange tube stretched tight between them across the whole frame; the astronaut leans back further and further with boots skidding on the mat, cheeks puffing red inside the helmet, while the saucer tilts and strains, the alien gripping its steering stick with both hands. The tube stretches thinner and thinner, a frozen beat of quivering tension. 4.3 to 5.0s: SNAP. The second 肚 is spoken at about 4.4s exactly as the tube lets go: the astronaut flies backwards onto its bottom on the left edge, the saucer spins and the confused tractor beam lifts the alien's own saucer and plops it down on the right edge. The released tube splits into two bouncing lengths that spring into the center: the left length folds into the 月 half, a tall rounded shape with two short inner bars, and the right length folds into the 土 half, a vertical stroke with a short upper and long lower horizontal, so the two halves land side by side as the correctly formed glyph 肚 in bold saturated orange-red, filling about 70% of frame height, centered and uncropped. Final hold 5.0 to 8.0s: the glyph 肚 stays perfectly still and fully readable. At about 5.8s the word 肚子 is spoken while the astronaut, sitting off to the left and never touching the strokes, pats its own suit and a round cartoon belly pops out under its hands; it grins and gives the belly two happy rubs, and the little alien on the right copies it with a tiny green belly pat. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly these syllables slowly and distinctly with clear tones, then stops: 肚、肚、肚子（ㄉㄨˋ、ㄉㄨˋ、ㄉㄨˋ ˙ㄗ）. No other speech, no English, no background music louder than the voice; only soft cartoon stretch, boing and plop sounds, nothing loud or startling. Keep 肚 as the one and only piece of text on screen, correctly formed with every stroke legible; no vocabulary text, no subtitles, no watermark. No real people, no realistic human figures, no flashing effects.

conceptZh: 調皮小老鼠把仰躺打盹的太空人玩偶圓鼓鼓的肚皮當彈簧床，第一次只彈起一點點，第二次用力一跳就被高高彈飛，飛過起司塔、撞上牆、倒栽蔥掉進水桶，被撞散的起司條叮叮咚咚落下，排成「肚」字。
object: a sleeping astronaut toy lying on its back whose big round puffy belly works as a trampoline, plus a wobbly tower of long yellow cheese sticks topped with a cheese wedge
morph: the mouse, launched off the belly, clips the cheese-stick tower in mid-flight; the loose sticks tumble and settle side by side as the 月 component on the left and the 土 component on the right, forming one correctly built 肚
creativeAngle: 先前的版本是撲滿、餅乾、拔河，這次換成「發射」：發射台就是肚皮本身，讓「肚皮」這個詞成為整個笑點的引擎，第三個詞說出時，觀眾正看到小老鼠在圓肚皮上彈跳，聽到的和看到的完全一致。選用肚皮（ㄆㄧˊ單一讀音，沒有輕聲），讀音穩定。起司條分成左右兩堆落下，清楚分出月和土兩個部件。
promptEn:
An 8-second slapstick animated clip, bright pastel look, soft even daylight, no dark grading. Setting: a plain pale mint floor and a pale cream wall, nothing busy behind. Lead: a tiny cheeky original cartoon mouse with big round ears, lightning fast and always grinning. Supporting character: a bouncy astronaut toy in a fishbowl helmet, napping on its back on the left with a huge round puffy belly pointing up. On the right stands a wobbly tower of long yellow cheese sticks with a cheese wedge on top. An empty toy bucket sits at the far right.

0–1.5s: The mouse zips in, stares up at the cheese wedge, licks its lips, then spots the astronaut's round belly, scrambles on top and strikes a drumroll pose, tiny fists pattering on the belly.
1.5–3.0s: First try. The mouse hops, the belly gives a soft boing, and it rises only a little before flopping back down; the first 肚 is spoken at about 1.6s on that small bounce. The astronaut drifts up off the floor in its sleep, its helmet bonks softly on nothing, and it sinks back down.
3.0–4.5s: The mouse crouches low, freezes for one beat of anticipation, then leaps with all its might. The belly squashes deep and springs back with a huge BOING, launching the mouse in a big arc across the frame. It overshoots the cheese wedge completely, clips the cheese-stick tower, bounces off the far wall with a squash, and drops upside down into the bucket, little legs kicking.
4.5–5.0s: The knocked-loose cheese sticks tumble into the center and settle in two groups: on the left, the 月 component, with a curving left stroke, a top bar joined to a hooked right stroke, and two short inner bars; on the right, the 土 component, with a short upper bar, a vertical stroke and a long bottom bar. Together they form one correctly built 肚 in bold saturated golden-orange, filling about 70% of frame height, centered and uncropped. The second 肚 is spoken at about 4.6s as the last stick clicks into place.
Final hold 5.0–8.0s: The glyph 肚 stays perfectly still. The mouse pops out of the bucket wearing the cheese wedge like a hat and grins. At about 5.8s the word 肚皮 is spoken as the astronaut, at the left edge, wakes, pats its round puffy belly and the mouse dashes back for one happy boing on it, nowhere near the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly these syllables slowly and distinctly with clear tones, then stops: 肚、肚、肚皮（ㄉㄨˋ、ㄉㄨˋ、ㄉㄨˋ ㄆㄧˊ）. No other speech, no English, only soft boing, bonk and plop sounds below the voice. 肚 is the only text on screen; no subtitles, no watermark. No real people, no flashing.
